definitions.explanation: Plants that grow in the sea, used in Japanese cuisine and other applications.

examples.english: Seaweed is good for your health.

⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{海藻|かいそう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{養殖|ようしょく}→養殖：08648_youshoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{盛|さか}んだ→盛ん：01239_sakan⟧。

examples.english: Japan has a long tradition of eating seaweed, with a wide variety including kombu and wakame.

notes:
TYPES:
Common edible seaweeds in Japan:
・⟦{昆布|こんぶ}→昆布：04934_konbu⟧ (kombu/kelp) - used for dashi
・⟦わかめ→わかめ：10654_wakame⟧ (wakame) - used in miso soup, salads
・⟦{海苔|のり}→海苔：10391_nori⟧ (nori) - used for sushi, onigiri
・⟦ひじき→ひじき：07971_hijiki⟧ (hijiki) - dark seaweed, often simmered
・⟦もずく→もずく：28690_mozuku⟧ (mozuku) - slimy seaweed, eaten with vinegar
・⟦めかぶ→めかぶ：noentry⟧ (mekabu) - root of ⟦わかめ→わかめ：10654_wakame⟧

USAGE:
・{海藻|かいそう}⟦サラダ→サラダ：01364_sarada⟧ (seaweed salad)
・⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧{海藻|かいそう} (dried seaweed)
・{海藻|かいそう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{採|と}る→採る：20862_toru⟧ (to harvest seaweed)

NUTRITION:
Seaweed is valued in Japan for its minerals (iodine, calcium), fiber, and umami. It is a staple of ⟦{和食|わしょく}→和食：10436_washoku⟧ (traditional Japanese cuisine).

NOTE:
Not to be confused with the homophone ⟦{海草|かいそう}→海草：noentry⟧ (sea grass), a flowering marine plant rather than an alga.
